name: wavelet_decomposition_v1
author: claude_strategist
mechanism: NIFTY's 5-second price series has genuine multi-scale structure: sub-10s microstructure noise (order book flicker, partial fills), 20–80s directional bursts from institutional algo legs, and session-level drift. By applying a Haar wavelet level-3 approximation (equivalent to an 8-bar = 40s simple moving average), we separate the 'tradeable band' (20–80s cycles) from tick noise, producing a denoised trend line. When the raw NIFTY price crosses above this denoised line AND the denoised slope is rising, it means a momentum burst has emerged cleanly from noise — sustained institutional TWAP/VWAP order flow has pushed price above its own smoothed trend, signaling continuation over the next 30–90 seconds. Detail energy (std of raw-vs-denoised divergence) filters out choppy, flat markets where crossovers are meaningless noise events.

indicators.name: denoised_sma8
indicators.purpose: 8-bar × 5s = 40s moving average = Haar wavelet level-3 approximation. This is NOT blind scaling (12× would give 168 bars). Instead: at 5s bars, wavelet level-3 captures 8–16 bar cycles (40–80s), precisely our hold time window. The original's 64-bar DWT on 1-min bars targeted 4–16 bar detail cycles (4–16 min) relative to a 10–30 min hold. We compress to 40s because we target the fast 30–90s momentum burst, not multi-minute continuation. Shorter lookback = more sensitive to current micro-momentum.

indicators.name: denoised_slope_bps
indicators.purpose: Rate of change of the denoised trend over 4 bars = 20s, expressed in bps. The original used linreg_slope over 5 1-min bars = 5 min. We compress to 20s slope window because we're trading the fast momentum burst — if the denoised slope over the last 20s is not already trending, the signal is stale. This is the direction confirmation filter: denoised must be actively trending, not just casually above/below raw price.

indicators.name: detail_energy_bps
indicators.purpose: Standard deviation of (raw minus denoised) over 16 bars = 80s, in bps. Approximates the level-2 and level-3 detail coefficient energy from the original strategy. Low energy = flat/dead market where crossovers are noise artifacts. High energy = active medium-frequency oscillation where the crossover signal is meaningful. 16-bar window covers one full 80s cycle, enough to distinguish active from quiet periods. Replaces the original's Detail_Energy_L2 which used pywt coefficient squaring — this std-based proxy is equivalent for binary filtering.

indicators.name: vwap_session
indicators.formula: cumulative_vwap(open, high, low, close, volume) from session open
indicators.purpose: Session VWAP as trend context filter. The original required close > vwap for long entries. Retained because NIFTY trades above session VWAP signal sustained buy-side institutional participation — cross-VWAP entries in wavelet uptrends have better follow-through as algo order flow is directionally aligned.

conditions: close crosses above denoised_sma8 (raw price emerges above 40s denoised trend)
denoised_slope_bps > slope_threshold (denoised trend actively rising in last 20s)
detail_energy_bps > min_energy_threshold (active medium-frequency cycle, not flat market)
close > vwap_session (bullish VWAP context — institutional buy-side flow)
buy_ce.confirmation: All four conditions satisfied at same bar

conditions: close crosses below denoised_sma8 (raw price drops below 40s denoised trend)
denoised_slope_bps < -slope_threshold (denoised trend actively falling in last 20s)
close < vwap_session (bearish VWAP context — institutional sell-side flow)
buy_pe.confirmation: All four conditions satisfied at same bar

exit.stop_rationale: NIFTY in a 30–90s hold typically moves 2–7 option pts (ATM delta ~0.5). A 4-pt stop = ~8 NIFTY spot points — if price retraces 8 pts against the wavelet crossover signal within seconds, the momentum burst thesis is invalidated. Tight enough to cut false crossovers quickly; wide enough to survive 15–20 NIFTY pt microstructure wobble.
exit.target_rationale: NIFTY momentum bursts flagged by wavelet crossover (genuine medium-frequency cycle active) typically extend 15–25 spot pts = 7–12 option pts. Target 7 pts captures the lower end of that range with 1:1.75 R:R, matching the win_rate_estimate of ~55% needed for net profitability.

filters.vix_filter: none (VIX not used — wavelet denoising self-adapts to volatility regime)
filters.time_filter: 09:30–15:20 IST; skip first 15 minutes (09:15–09:30) to allow 120-bar warmup and avoid opening noise
filters.volume_filter: none explicitly — detail_energy_bps implicitly filters low-activity bars
filters.trend_filter: close vs session VWAP for bullish/bearish context
filters.spread_filter: none — limit order execution at close prices

edge.edge_decay_risk: Moderate — wavelet crossover on a 40s SMA is conceptually similar to price-crosses-SMA signals which are well-known; the edge comes from the detail energy filter requiring active medium-frequency oscillation, which is less commonly implemented at 5s resolution

adaptation_notes: Original used pywt.wavedec (db4, 3-level) on 1-min equity bars with 64-bar minimum lookback (64 min of data). Converted to: (1) Haar-equivalent level-3 approximation = simple 8-bar SMA at 5s — same mathematical result for uniformly-sampled data without pywt dependency; (2) Compressed to 5-second bars targeting 30–90s hold vs original 10–30 min — indicators compressed proportionally; (3) VWAP filter retained from original but session VWAP on NIFTY index replaces per-stock VWAP; (4) Universe narrowed from NIFTY 50 equities to NIFTY index itself — the wavelet denoising principle is index-agnostic and actually cleaner on the index since NIFTY is smoother and less gappy than individual stocks; (5) Detail energy proxy changed from pywt coefficient energy ratio to rolling std of raw-vs-denoised — equivalent for binary filtering purposes; (6) Stops/targets converted from percentage-based (20/35 bps on equity) to absolute option premium points calibrated to NIFTY ATM option move magnitudes at 30–90s horizons.
weaknesses: 8-bar SMA crossover on NIFTY can whipsaw in choppy sessions — detail energy filter partially mitigates but won't eliminate false signals during news-driven noise
Haar approximation is a weaker denoising method than db4 wavelet used in original — genuine wavelet with pywt would give marginally sharper signal separation, especially at level boundaries
VWAP filter creates signal asymmetry: bullish signals only when above VWAP, bearish only below. In trending sessions this is excellent; in range-bound sessions it misses mean-reversion opportunities
Denoised slope over 20s can lag real momentum shifts — a fast gap-and-go move will trigger the raw-crosses-denoised entry but the slope may still be stale for 1–2 bars
